# Aim

Establish the **exact** AnnData (`.h5ad`) format that exploreDE will consume,
based on the current app's actual requirements. This document freezes the
schema; subsequent plans will cover the migration, loader refactor, and
validator.

Scope of this document: **schema only**. Not migration steps, not UI changes,
not a roadmap.

# Goals

1. **One container for all omics.** Genomics (bulk RNA, CRISPR CountQC),
   proteomics (protein / peptide / PTM), metabolomics, lipidomics — all read
   through the same code path.
2. **Detach from SUSHI / B-Fabric.** No `param$*` requirement. No reliance on
   gStore paths, `[Factor]` column suffixes, or `constrast_` rowData nesting.
   All experimental design information lives inside the AnnData object itself.
3. **Public-ready.** A researcher with their own counts CSV + sample CSV must
   be able to build an AnnData that loads cleanly.
4. **Preserve everything the app currently does.** Every tab, every plot,
   every filter must keep working. No feature loss from the migration.
5. **Respect the `feature_id` refactor (2026-03-12).** `feature_id` remains
   the universal unique row key (`var_names` in AnnData).

# Non-goals

- Compatibility shim for reading legacy SE objects — that belongs in a separate
  migration plan.
- MuData (multi-modal) support — the container harmonises the **schema** for
  all omics types but each `.h5ad` still holds one modality. Cross-modality
  joining comes later.
- Changing UI / plot behaviour.
- Interactive AnnData editing.

# Axis convention — the critical flip

SummarizedExperiment is **features × samples** (rows × cols). AnnData is
**samples × features** (obs × var). Every matrix transposes on ingest.

| SE slot            | AnnData slot | Shape             |
|--------------------|--------------|-------------------|
| `assays()[[k]]`    | `layers[k]`  | `n_obs × n_vars`  |
| `colData`          | `obs`        | `n_obs × p_obs`   |
| `rowData`          | `var`        | `n_vars × p_var`  |
| `metadata`         | `uns`        | dict              |
| —                  | `obsm`       | sample embeddings |
| —                  | `varm`       | feature matrices  |

**Convention in this spec:** when examples show a matrix, rows are samples
unless explicitly noted.

# Top-level layout

```text
adata.X                       # primary assay (canonical for the modality)
adata.layers[<name>]          # all other assays (vst, log2, tpm, imputed, …)
adata.obs                     # sample metadata + experimental factors
adata.var                     # feature annotation (shared across contrasts)
adata.obsm["X_pca"], …        # cached sample embeddings (optional)
adata.varm["de_<contrast>"]   # per-contrast DE statistics (dense)
adata.uns["schema_version"]   # "exploreDE/1.0"
adata.uns["omics_type"]       # "rnaseq_bulk" | "proteomics" | …
adata.uns["hierarchy"]        # feature hierarchy declaration
adata.uns["design"]           # factors, grouping, formula hints
adata.uns["de"]               # per-contrast DE metadata (mirrors varm keys)
adata.uns["enrichment"]       # ORA / GSEA / KEGG / STRING results
adata.uns["provenance"]       # who/when/what produced this object
```

# `adata.X` and `adata.layers`

## Primary assay (`X`)

Exactly one matrix lives in `X`. It is the **canonical input** for the
modality — the matrix that statistical methods would consume by default.

| Modality           | `X` contains             | Typical dtype        |
|--------------------|--------------------------|----------------------|
| `rnaseq_bulk`      | raw integer counts       | int32 / sparse CSR   |
| `crispr_countqc`   | raw sgRNA counts         | int32                |
| `proteomics`       | transformed intensities  | float32              |
| `metabolomics`     | normalised intensities   | float32              |
| `lipidomics`       | normalised intensities   | float32              |

Rationale: proteomics pipelines (prolfqua, MaxLFQ) deliver
already-transformed values as the analysis-ready matrix; raw intensities are
preserved alongside in `layers["intensities_raw"]`. For RNA-seq, raw counts
stay in `X` so DESeq2/edgeR-style downstream work remains trivial.

## Additional assays (`layers`)

Any other matrix shape-compatible with `X`. Names are lower-case, no spaces.
The current app needs (at minimum) the following layer names to be **reserved
and recognised** when present:

| Layer key            | Meaning                                               |
|----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| `counts`             | raw integer counts (RNA-seq / CRISPR)                 |
| `normalised`         | size-factor / library-normalised (replaces SUSHI `signal` / `xNorm`) |
| `log2`               | `log2(normalised + pseudocount)`                      |
| `vst`                | `DESeq2::varianceStabilizingTransformation()`         |
| `tpm`                | transcripts per million (RNA-seq only)                |
| `fpkm`               | fragments per kb per million (RNA-seq only)           |
| `intensities_raw`    | raw MS intensities (proteomics / metabolomics)        |
| `intensities_norm`   | normalised intensities                                |
| `imputed`            | imputed intensities                                   |
| `nr_peptides`        | peptides per protein per sample (proteomics)          |
| `present_flag`       | logical/0-1 matrix (CRISPR CountQC `presentFlag`)     |

Any other layer is allowed but not specially interpreted.

**Distribution detection stays runtime** (per the 2025-10-02 spec):
skewness + kurtosis classification selects log vs linear plot scales — not
encoded in names.

## Sparse storage

`X` and `layers` MAY be sparse (CSR in AnnData's default convention). Raw
RNA-seq counts and CRISPR counts SHOULD be sparse for space. Proteomics
intensities are usually dense.

# `adata.obs` — sample metadata

`obs_names` (the index) are sample identifiers — matching colnames of the
original assay matrices. They must be unique, string-typed, and stable across
the object's lifetime.

## Required columns

| Column                  | Type             | Notes                                     |
|-------------------------|------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| `sample_label`          | string           | human-readable display name               |

## Experimental factors (`factor_*`)

All experimental design covariates are declared with the `factor_` prefix.
This replaces the SUSHI `[Factor]` column-name suffix.

| Column pattern   | Type           | Examples                             |
|------------------|----------------|--------------------------------------|
| `factor_<name>`  | categorical    | `factor_condition`, `factor_batch`, `factor_genotype`, `factor_sex` |
| `factor_<name>`  | numeric        | `factor_timepoint`, `factor_age`     |

Rules:

- Column levels for categorical factors are declared via pandas `Categorical`
  with explicit `categories=` to preserve ordering. (`anndataR` in R maps
  this to `factor()` with `levels=` on read.)
- The app infers available factors by scanning for the `factor_` prefix. No
  allow-list in `uns` required — but one may be supplied (see
  `uns["design"]`).

## Optional convention columns

| Column                  | Type       | Notes                                       |
|-------------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------|
| `organism`              | string     | e.g. `"Homo sapiens"`                       |
| `feature_level`         | string     | `"gene"`, `"isoform"`, `"protein"`, `"peptide"`, `"phosphosite"`, `"compound"` — sample-level *declaration* of what the features represent |
| `sample_type`           | string     | `"biological"`, `"qc"`, `"blank"`, `"pool"` |
| `bfabric_sample_id`     | string     | optional external ID                        |
| `label_*`               | any        | any annotation for plots/tables (library size, creatinine, collection date …) |

`sample_type` replaces the implicit "all samples are biological" assumption
and lets the loader filter QC/blanks out of DE plots without code branching
per modality.

## Migration from current `param$sampleGroup` / `param$refGroup`

These two are **deprecated as top-level fields**. Test vs. reference
assignment per contrast now lives in `uns["de"][<contrast>]` (see §
"Differential expression"). The colData itself only holds the factors; the
contrast spec lives with the contrast.

# `adata.var` — feature annotation

`var_names` (the index) = **`feature_id`**, the universal unique key
established in the 2026-03-12 refactor. Format:

- RNA-seq (gene-level): `scuttle::uniquifyFeatureNames(gene_id, gene_name)`
- Proteomics (protein-level): `protein_Id` if unique
- Proteomics (peptide/PTM): `build_feature_id()` output, e.g.
  `A0A2R8Y4L2_A0A2R8Y4L2_S199_SGsGNFGGGR`
- Metabolomics: `compound_id` or `m_z_rt` string

## Required columns

| Column        | Type   | Notes                                                            |
|---------------|--------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `description` | string | free-text, searchable, SUSHI `[Source]...` tail stripped on ingest |

## Canonical identifier columns (`label_*`)

All identifier columns use the `label_` prefix. None are required; all that
are present are exposed as optional column-visibility toggles in the DE table
and as search targets in the feature selector.

| Column                     | Applies to            |
|----------------------------|-----------------------|
| `label_gene_symbol`        | all                   |
| `label_gene_id`            | RNA-seq (Ensembl)     |
| `label_transcript_id`      | RNA-seq isoform       |
| `label_entrez_id`          | all                   |
| `label_ensembl_gene_id`    | all                   |
| `label_uniprot_id`         | proteomics            |
| `label_flydb_id`           | fly datasets          |
| `label_biotype`            | RNA-seq               |
| `label_chromosome`         | all (for locus plots) |
| `label_assignment_method`  | metabolomics / PTM    |
| `label_nr_peptides`        | proteomics            |
| `label_global_base_mean`   | all                   |
| `label_go_bp` / `_mf` / `_cc` | RNA-seq            |

## Hierarchy columns (`hierarchy_*`)

For proteomics and PTM data, the sub-feature lineage is encoded with
`hierarchy_` columns. **Each column alone may contain duplicates; the
combination of all hierarchy columns uniquely identifies each row.** The
declared order is coarsest → finest.

| Column                    | Meaning                                    |
|---------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| `hierarchy_protein`       | protein identifier                         |
| `hierarchy_peptide`       | peptide sequence                           |
| `hierarchy_peptidoform`   | modified peptide sequence                  |
| `hierarchy_site`          | PTM site (e.g. `S199`)                     |
| `hierarchy_multiplicity`  | integer — PTMs per peptide                 |
| `hierarchy_ion`           | precursor ion (`mz_charge`)                |

The order is declared in `uns["hierarchy"]["levels"]` (see §
"Unstructured metadata"). For RNA-seq the hierarchy is trivially
`["gene"]` (or `["gene", "transcript"]` for isoform-level).

## Per-feature display columns (`display_*`)

Per the display_label_plan. Optional:

| Column                   | Notes                                                 |
|--------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| `display_label_primary`  | what to show in plots/tables by default               |
| `display_label_secondary`| shown on hover/tooltip                                |

If absent, the app falls back to `label_gene_symbol` → `feature_id`.

# `adata.varm` — per-contrast DE statistics

**Design decision:** DE results per contrast go in `varm`, keyed
`de_<contrast>`. Each entry is a dense `n_vars × k` table. This is the
AnnData-native place for per-feature, per-contrast statistics and mirrors
scanpy's convention for gene-group results.

## Required columns in each `varm["de_<contrast>"]`

| Column          | Type    | Notes                                                     |
|-----------------|---------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| `effect_log2fc` | float   | log2 fold change — volcano x-axis                         |
| `score_pvalue`  | float   | raw p-value — volcano y-axis                              |
| `score_fdr`     | float   | adjusted p / q-value — significance threshold             |

## Optional columns (surface in DE table column-visibility)

| Column                  | Type          | Notes                                         |
|-------------------------|---------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| `effect_<other>`        | float         | alternate effect sizes (e.g. `effect_difference` for proteomics) |
| `score_<other>`         | float         | `score_t_statistic`, `score_wald_stat`, …     |
| `label_base_mean`       | float         | DE-specific mean (MA plot y-axis)             |
| `label_ave_log_cpm`     | float         | edgeR MA plot alternative                     |
| `label_n_missing`       | int           | missing-value count (proteomics)              |
| `label_ci_lower` / `_upper` | float     | confidence interval bounds                   |
| `label_se`              | float         | standard error                                |
| `label_direction`       | string        | pre-computed "up"/"down"/"ns" for convenience |

**Column order matters** for the default DE-table view: first `effect_*`,
then `score_*`, then `label_*`. Implementation enforces this on read.

## Per-assay group-mean columns

The current app computes `<assay>_<group>_Mean` and `<assay>_<group>_SD`
columns on load. Under AnnData these are **still computed on the fly** from
`layers` + `uns["de"][<contrast>]["test_group"]` / `["reference_group"]` —
they do NOT need to be baked into `varm`. This keeps contrast tables lean.

# `adata.obsm` — sample-space embeddings (optional)

Precomputed embeddings to avoid re-running on every app launch.

| Key           | Shape             | Contents                          |
|---------------|-------------------|-----------------------------------|
| `X_pca`       | `n_obs × k`       | principal components              |
| `X_umap`      | `n_obs × 2`       | UMAP                              |
| `X_mds`       | `n_obs × k`       | MDS                               |
| `X_tsne`      | `n_obs × 2`       | t-SNE                             |

Companion metadata (variance explained, method params) goes in
`uns["embeddings"][<key>]`.

# `adata.uns` — unstructured metadata

A nested dict. Keys below are either required (R) or optional (O). Missing
optional keys → app uses sensible defaults.

## `schema_version` (R)

String. Must equal `"exploreDE/1.0"` for this spec. Bumps on breaking changes.

## `omics_type` (R)

One of:

- `"rnaseq_bulk"`
- `"crispr_countqc"`
- `"proteomics"` (subtypes declared via `feature_level` in `obs`)
- `"metabolomics"`
- `"lipidomics"`
- `"atac_bulk"` (future)

## `hierarchy` (R)

```yaml
hierarchy:
  levels: ["protein", "peptide", "site"]   # maps to hierarchy_* var cols
  unit:   "site"                            # which level a single row represents
```

For RNA-seq: `{ levels: ["gene"], unit: "gene" }`.

## `design` (O, strongly recommended)

```yaml
design:
  factors: ["factor_condition", "factor_batch"]   # primary + nuisance
  grouping: "factor_condition"                    # default colour-by in plots
  formula: "~ factor_batch + factor_condition"    # advisory only
```

If absent, the loader infers `factors` by scanning `obs` for the `factor_`
prefix and picks the first as `grouping`. Explicit declaration is
recommended for non-trivial designs.

## `de` (R, one entry per contrast)

The DE metadata dict. Keys mirror the `varm["de_<contrast>"]` names (no
`de_` prefix here).

```yaml
de:
  treatment_vs_control:
    assay_used:        "vst"                    # which layer/X drove DE
    factor_used:       ["factor_condition", "factor_batch"]
    test_group:        "treatment"              # replaces param$sampleGroup
    reference_group:   "control"                # replaces param$refGroup
    contrast_formula:  "factor_condition_treatment - factor_condition_control"
    model:             "DESeq2"                 # or limma, edgeR, prolfqua, msqrob2 …
    n_test:            12
    n_reference:       12
  OT_vs_Manual:
    assay_used:        "transformedData"
    factor_used:       ["factor_condition"]
    test_group:        "OT"
    reference_group:   "Manual"
    contrast_formula:  "OT - Manual"
    model:             "prolfqua"
```

Required fields per contrast: `assay_used`, `factor_used`, `test_group`,
`reference_group`. All others optional.

## `enrichment` (R where available, one entry per contrast)

Pathway / enrichment analysis results are a **first-class, uniform
requirement across all omics**, not a genomics-only convenience. Proteomics,
metabolomics, and lipidomics objects must carry enrichment results in the
same slot, with the same shape, as genomics. If enrichment has not yet been
run for a modality, the exporter is responsible for running it before
producing the `.h5ad`.

### Target: clusterProfiler parity for all omics

The reference implementation is `clusterProfiler` — specifically its
`enrichResult` (ORA) and `gseaResult` (GSEA) objects, as already produced
for genomics under the SUSHI pipeline. The aim in the first phase is to
deliver clusterProfiler-equivalent outputs for **every** omics modality:

- **Genomics (RNA-seq, CRISPR):** already runs `clusterProfiler::enrichGO`,
  `clusterProfiler::gseGO`, `clusterProfiler::enrichKEGG`, etc. No change in
  upstream computation — only in storage location.
- **Proteomics:** currently ships **no** enrichment. Exporter must generate
  clusterProfiler results from the DE contrast, mapping
  `label_uniprot_id` → Entrez via `bitr()` (or equivalent) before calling
  `enrichGO` / `gseGO` / `enrichKEGG`.
- **Metabolomics / lipidomics (future):** clusterProfiler
  `enrichPathway` / custom `enricher()` with KEGG compound sets, HMDB
  classifications, or LipidMaps categories. Same storage slot, same
  downstream app code.

Downstream app code (the ORA / GSEA / KEGG tabs) must not branch on omics
type — it reads `uns["enrichment"][<contrast>][<method>]` uniformly.

### Storage — dual mode

Each contrast holds one dict of method → result. Two storage modes
co-exist:

1. **Native clusterProfiler object, serialised** (primary for R loader,
   lossless):
   ```
   uns["enrichment_native"][<contrast>][<method>]
   ```
   An `enrichResult` or `gseaResult` R object, serialised as raw bytes in
   `.h5ad`. The R loader unserialises these directly and feeds them to the
   existing plotting / table code with zero translation.

2. **Tidy DataFrame mirror** (for portability + Python readers + diffing):
   ```yaml
   enrichment:
     treatment_vs_control:
       ora_up:   <DataFrame>
       ora_down: <DataFrame>
       gsea:     <DataFrame>
       kegg:     <DataFrame>
       reactome: <DataFrame>           # optional, if run
   ```
   Columns: `category`, `id`, `description`, `n_genes_mapped`,
   `n_genes_in_set`, `gene_ratio`, `bg_ratio`, `enrichment_score`, `nes`,
   `pvalue`, `p_adjust`, `q_value`, `method`, `ontology`, `feature_ids`
   (list-col of `var_names`), `feature_labels` (list-col of gene symbols).

Exporters SHOULD write both; the R loader prefers native, Python readers
read tidy. If only one is present, the app degrades gracefully.

### Method keys (reserved)

| Key         | clusterProfiler call                    |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------|
| `ora_up`    | `enrichGO` / `enrichKEGG` on up-regulated genes   |
| `ora_down`  | `enrichGO` / `enrichKEGG` on down-regulated genes |
| `ora_all`   | `enrichGO` on all DE genes (non-directional)      |
| `gsea`      | `gseGO` / `gseKEGG` ranked by `effect_log2fc`     |
| `kegg`      | `enrichKEGG` / `gseKEGG`                          |
| `reactome`  | `ReactomePA::enrichPathway` / `gsePathway`        |
| `string`    | STRING-DB (for future network views)              |

Additional keys allowed; app renders whatever is present.

### Inputs no longer stored

The current app's `metadata$enrichInput` (the `log2Ratio` named vector,
`selections$upGenes` / `downGenes`, and `seqAnno`) is **derived on the fly**
under the new schema — not stored. When a tab needs those inputs (e.g.
re-running enrichment with a different threshold interactively), they are
reconstructed from `varm["de_<contrast>"]` + `var` + `uns["de"][<contrast>]`
+ `uns["app_hints"]` thresholds.

## `provenance` (O but strongly recommended for public release)

```yaml
provenance:
  created_utc:         "2026-04-17T14:22:00Z"
  created_by:          "exploreDE-export v0.3.2"
  source_format:       "SummarizedExperiment"
  source_path:         "/srv/gstore/projects/p3009/…"   # may be null for user uploads
  converter_version:   "anndata-export/1.0"
  notes:               "Converted from SUSHI DESeq2 output."
```

## `app_hints` (O)

```yaml
app_hints:
  default_contrast:    "treatment_vs_control"
  default_assay:       "vst"
  fdr_threshold:       0.05
  log2fc_threshold:    1.0
  go_fdr_threshold:    0.1
```

Hints only — the app UI always lets the user override.

# Data-type-specific notes

## RNA-seq bulk

- `X` = raw counts (sparse int32)
- Required layers: none (all derived in-app if missing), but typically:
  `normalised`, `log2`, `vst`, optionally `tpm` / `fpkm`.
- Hierarchy: `["gene"]` or `["gene", "transcript"]`.

## CRISPR CountQC

- `X` = raw sgRNA counts.
- Required layer: `present_flag` (replaces SE `assay(se, "presentFlag")`).
- `var` additional columns: `label_sgrna_sequence`, `label_target_gene`
  (for `collapse_guides_to_genes()`).
- `obs` may include `label_library_size` to avoid recomputation.

## Proteomics

- `X` = transformed / analysis-ready intensities (prolfqua output).
- Required layers: `intensities_raw`, optionally `intensities_norm`,
  `imputed`, `nr_peptides`.
- Hierarchy declares the level actually in `var` — `["protein"]`,
  `["protein", "peptide"]`, `["protein", "site", "multiplicity"]`, etc.
- `var` retains domain columns: `label_uniprot_id`, `label_gene_symbol`,
  `label_nr_peptides`, plus any `hierarchy_*`.
- Multiple contrasts native — one `varm["de_<contrast>"]` per contrast, not
  nested DataFrames in `var`.

## Metabolomics / lipidomics (future)

- `X` = normalised intensities.
- `var`: `label_compound`, `label_inchi_key`, `label_hmdb_id`,
  `label_lipidmaps_id`, `label_mz`, `label_retention_time`,
  `label_assignment_method` (MS1 / MS2 / manual).
- `obs`: `sample_type` critical — distinguishes QC / blank / pool.
- DE storage identical to proteomics.

# SUSHI decoupling — what goes away

| Current (SUSHI coupling)                  | New (AnnData-native)                              |
|-------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| `metadata$param$sampleGroup` / `$refGroup`| `uns["de"][<c>]["test_group"]` / `["reference_group"]` |
| `metadata$param$comparison`               | contrast name = key of `uns["de"]`                |
| `metadata$param$groupingName`             | `uns["design"]["grouping"]`                       |
| `metadata$param$featureLevel`             | `obs["feature_level"]` + `uns["hierarchy"]["unit"]` |
| `metadata$param$backgroundExpression`     | pseudocount baked into `layers["log2"]` (or `uns["app_hints"]["log2_pseudocount"]`) |
| `metadata$param$refBuild`                 | `uns["reference_genome"]` (string only)           |
| `metadata$param$runGO` + `enrichResult` / `enrichResultGSEA` (genomics only) | `uns["enrichment_native"][<c>][<method>]` **for all omics**; tidy mirror in `uns["enrichment"][<c>][<method>]`. Proteomics exporters must run clusterProfiler before export to reach parity. |
| `metadata$param$samples` (subset filter)  | dropped — callers subset before export            |
| `[Factor]` column-name suffix             | `factor_` column-name prefix                      |
| `constrast_<c>` rowData nesting           | `varm["de_<c>"]`                                  |
| gStore/pStore URL discovery, LDAP         | out of loader — app accepts a local path or URL to `.h5ad` |
| RDS / QS2 file format                     | HDF5 (`.h5ad`); RDS accepted only through a one-way converter |

# Traceability: every current app read → AnnData slot

| Current code access                           | AnnData location                                              |
|-----------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| `assay(se, "counts")`                         | `layers["counts"]` (RNA/CRISPR) or `X`                        |
| `assay(se, "signal")` / `"xNorm"`             | `layers["normalised"]`                                        |
| `assay(se, "presentFlag")`                    | `layers["present_flag"]`                                      |
| computed `log2(normalised + pseudo)`          | `layers["log2"]`                                              |
| `getTpm(se)`, `getRpkm(se)`                   | `layers["tpm"]`, `layers["fpkm"]`                             |
| proteomics assays (rawData, transformedData)  | `X` = transformedData, `layers["intensities_raw"]` = rawData  |
| `colData$Name` / `Sample` / `sampleName`      | `obs_names`                                                   |
| `colData$<Factor>` columns (with `[Factor]`)  | `obs["factor_<name>"]`                                        |
| `param$sampleGroup`, `param$refGroup`         | `uns["de"][<c>]["test_group"]` / `["reference_group"]`        |
| `rowData$gene_id`, `gene_name`, `description` | `var["label_gene_id"]`, `var["label_gene_symbol"]`, `var["description"]` |
| `rowData$feature_id`                          | `var_names`                                                   |
| `rowData$type` (biotype)                      | `var["label_biotype"]`                                        |
| `rowData$GO BP` / `MF` / `CC`                 | `var["label_go_bp"]` / `_mf` / `_cc`                          |
| `rowData$constrast_<c>$log2Ratio` etc.        | `varm["de_<c>"]["effect_log2fc"]`                             |
| `rowData$log2Ratio` / `pValue` / `fdr` (genomics, single DE) | `varm["de_<c>"]["effect_log2fc"]` / `score_pvalue` / `score_fdr` |
| `param$comparison` (`"diff--over--undiff"`)   | contrast key in `uns["de"]`                                   |
| `param$runGO`, `enrichResult`, `enrichResultGSEA` | `uns["enrichment"][<c>][...]`                             |
| `metadata$enrichInput$seqAnno`                | derived from `var` at call-site                               |
| `metadata$enrichInput$log2Ratio`              | derived from `varm["de_<c>"]["effect_log2fc"]`                |
| `metadata$enrichInput$selections$upGenes`     | derived from `varm["de_<c>"]` + thresholds                    |
| `sgRNA_to_gene` (CRISPR)                      | `var["label_target_gene"]`                                    |

# Minimum viable AnnData (bring-your-own-data)

The smallest object that loads cleanly:

```r
library(anndataR)

adata <- AnnData(
  X      = counts_matrix,                    # samples × features
  obs    = data.frame(
             row.names    = sample_ids,
             sample_label = sample_ids,
             factor_condition = factor(c("ctrl","ctrl","trt","trt"))
           ),
  var    = data.frame(
             row.names   = feature_ids,
             description = descriptions
           ),
  uns    = list(
    schema_version = "exploreDE/1.0",
    omics_type     = "rnaseq_bulk",
    hierarchy      = list(levels = "gene", unit = "gene"),
    design         = list(factors = "factor_condition",
                          grouping = "factor_condition"),
    de             = list()    # empty → app still loads, DE tabs gracefully disabled
  )
)

anndataR::write_h5ad(adata, "my_experiment.h5ad")
```

Adding a contrast is a matter of populating `varm["de_<name>"]` and
`uns["de"][<name>]`.

# Validator

A dedicated validator (follow-on work) will:

1. Verify `schema_version == "exploreDE/1.0"`.
2. Check `omics_type` is from the allowed set.
3. Confirm `obs_names` and `var_names` are unique strings.
4. For each `varm["de_*"]`: require `effect_log2fc`, `score_pvalue`,
   `score_fdr`; row count == `n_vars`; key exists in `uns["de"]`.
5. For each `uns["de"][<c>]`: require `assay_used`, `factor_used`,
   `test_group`, `reference_group`; `assay_used` resolves to `X` or a layer
   key; `factor_used` entries exist in `obs`; `test_group` / `reference_group`
   are levels of `obs[factor_used[1]]`.
6. Warn on `factor_` columns not listed in `uns["design"]["factors"]` (and
   vice versa).
7. Warn on hierarchy columns missing a declaration in
   `uns["hierarchy"]["levels"]`.

Mirror of the existing `validate_summarized_experiment.R`, rewritten for
AnnData in R (via `anndataR`) with an equivalent Python version for users
producing `.h5ad` outside R.

# Open questions — to resolve with WEW before freezing

1. **`X` vs `layers["counts"]` as canonical for RNA-seq.** Bioconductor
   convention is "raw in X, derived in layers" (what scanpy also does),
   which we've picked. Scanpy users sometimes put log-normalised in X and
   raw in `layers["counts"]`. Either is fine — we pick raw-in-X for
   symmetry with proteomics (where the analysis-ready matrix is in X).
   → **Confirm.**

2. **Enrichment: tidy DataFrame vs native object.** Tidy is portable,
   clusterProfiler-native is lossless. Decision (2026-04-17): write both
   when an `enrichResult` / `gseaResult` exists; R loader prefers native,
   Python readers read tidy. → **Confirm dual storage is acceptable
   size-wise.** Follow-up: inventory the proteomics ID → Entrez mapping
   path (UniProt → Entrez via `bitr()` / `AnnotationDbi`) so the proteomics
   exporter can actually run clusterProfiler.

3. **`display_label_*` vs computing display at load.** The display_label_plan
   (2026-03-xx) is still in flux. This spec reserves the columns but does
   not require them. → **Align with display_label_plan outcome.**

4. **Multi-SE (`server-multi-*`) future.** Do multi-dataset tabs read
   multiple `.h5ad` files, or a single MuData / anndata collection? Out of
   scope here, but the schema is chosen so either works.

5. **Numeric factors.** AnnData obs columns must be categorical OR numeric
   — there's no native "factor with ordered levels" dtype in Python. For
   ordered categorical factors (e.g. timepoint = 0, 2, 4, 8h) we rely on
   pandas `CategoricalDtype(ordered=True)`. → **Verify anndataR round-trip
   preserves ordering.**

6. **Sparse vs dense for proteomics.** Proteomics intensity matrices have
   MNAR missingness but are otherwise dense — keep dense with NaN? Or
   sparse with explicit NaN encoding? → **Dense + NaN preferred unless
   memory becomes a problem.**

7. **Contrast naming convention.** Free-form string keys are flexible but
   allow collisions and messy UI. Propose: `<test>_vs_<reference>`,
   lower-case, `[a-z0-9_]` only. → **Confirm and enforce in validator.**

# Follow-on plans (not in this document)

- `anndata_migration_plan_<date>.qmd` — loader refactor, SE-to-AnnData
  converter for legacy SUSHI outputs, phased cut-over per tab, regression
  test matrix against the 4 canonical datasets.
- `anndata_validator_<date>.qmd` — R + Python validator implementation.
- `anndata_byod_guide_<date>.qmd` — public-facing "bring your own data"
  guide with worked examples per omics type.
- `byod_from_csv_<date>.qmd` — helper that takes `counts.csv` +
  `samples.csv` + `features.csv` + optional `de_<contrast>.csv` and
  produces a conformant `.h5ad`.
